title: Teaching himself ragtime in F-sharp with a friend at age ten
summary: Wooding and a friend play rags in F-sharp and C-sharp on organ and borrowed pianos and hear local players like Jesse Pinkett and Jack the Bear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What I decided to do was, I wanted to play what was called ragtime then, because we didn't know anything else, so I had a friend of ours, and we got together and started playing these little rags, or what we could get together. First thing we started in. And the funny thing, all the music that I could read was in the key, like, F, C, E-flat and B-flat. But we started our rag in F-sharp. And we played F-sharp for quite awhile. You know, F-sharp is -- and C-sharp, then we got
on to C-sharp. I still can't play -- by, improvise in any kind of way, in the other keys. So --
How old were you at this point?
At this here, I was about ten.
Ten. And you were playing the piano or organ?
Oh, we were playing the organ. And when I could get to somebody's house that had a piano, we played the piano.
And what did -- was it a trio, or--

Well, this other fellow was trying to play the piano, too. So we had -- we used to go around and if he heard anything, he'd come in and tell me about it. And if I heard anything from somebody -- one of the great guys that was playing around there -- cause there were fellows playing. Like there was a fellow called Jesse Pinkett, and there was a fellow called Jack the Bear. So, they were playing and I'll tell you about another man a little later on -- that year, we went to Atlantic City again, because every summer he went to Atlantic City.
